chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to a man selling a dinar on credit for one hundred, and less or more."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell gold coins on credit for a higher price in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the permissibility of selling a gold dinar on credit for a fixed price, explicitly allowing the credit amount to be either higher or lower than the spot price. This ruling highlights the flexibility in deferred payment transactions (bay' al-nasi'ah) within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from strict riba prohibitions by focusing on the agreement of the specific deferred sum rather than a fixed exchange ratio.
